questions.question: In the demo, why did the 0-shot output {"category": "Refund Request"} fail validation?
options: The semantics were wrong — the model misread the ticket
Semantically right but the literal format drifted: Refund Request is not one of the agreed enum values
It emitted an explanation outside the JSON
It mistook an example for live input
questions.explanation: See the "Examples are the most direct behavioral spec" section: in the 0-shot call Refund Request is semantically right but format-drifted, not one of the agreed enum literals.

questions.question: When the demo swapped in an example set whose two entries were both billing, an obvious refund ticket came out as billing. What does this show?
options: Too few examples — ten or more are needed to cover the classes
Example format is the output template, so even casing gets imitated
Examples also teach classification boundaries: all-positive, class-skewed sets tell the model 'the answers mostly look like this'
Examples only work when placed right next to the real input
questions.explanation: See the "Diversity decides generalization" section: the demo's two billing-only examples dragged an obvious refund ticket into billing, because example diversity decides generalization.

questions.question: How many examples does the lesson say are usually enough to lock down the output format?
questions.explanation: See the "Quantity and cost trade off" section: usually two to five examples lock the format; beyond that you pay linearly growing cost for rare edges.
